newsitem.title: ITALY: Kidnapped Italians freed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped Italians freed in Chechnya.

text.p: Three Italian aid workers abducted in Chechnya have been released after being held for more than two months, the Italian Foreign Ministry said on Friday.
A statement said the three men were in good health. They had been flown to Moscow, where they were staying at the Italian embassy pending their return to Italy.
The ministry said the Italians were released overnight.

It said their freedom followed repeated talks between Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and the Russian authorities, as well as between the aid workers' organisation, INTER SOS, and "influential Chechen figures". It did not elaborate.
The three men, Sandro Pocaterra, 41, Augusto Lombardi, 36. and Giuseppe Valenti, 62, were last seen on September 26.

The ministry said they had been seized the next day near the Chechen capital Grozny, where they had been heading by car from Nazran in Ingushetia, a region bordering Chechnya, to deliver medicine and equipment to a war-damaged hospital.
Tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, have been killed in the conflict between Russian troops and Chechen separatists.
Fighting largely halted under a ceasefire last August but no solution has been found to the central dispute of whether or not Chechnya should remain part of Russia.
President Boris Yeltsin issued a controversial decree last Saturday ordering Russia's last units to leave Chechnya before planned regional elections.
